title: Kindness for Gran
lines: Gran had a sickness and stayed in bed.
Meg saw her and felt a big sadness.
Gran did not want to sit up at all.
Meg took her a doll to hold.
Gran said thank you, but still felt bad.
"What can I do?" Meg asked her dad.
"Gran likes soup," said Dad. "I will help."
Dad and Meg made hot soup in a pot.
Meg took it up the steps to Gran.
The room was dark, so Dad lit a lamp.
Gran ate it all and sat up tall.
"Your kindness made me well," said Gran.
Meg's sadness had turned into happiness.
Now Meg and Dad make soup each week.

questions.ask: What did Meg try first, and did it help?
questions.listenFor: She took Gran a doll to hold. Gran said thank you but still felt bad.

questions.ask: Who made the soup with Meg?
questions.listenFor: Her dad. He said Gran likes soup and that he would help. Sadness, happiness, kindness, sickness - -ness turns a describing word into a thing.

questions.ask: What would you do for someone at home who felt sad? Why?
questions.listenFor: Any kind answer counts. You are listening for the because part, not for a right idea.
